answer: Plant canary tasks. Each close, 1 in 20 prompts carries a hidden twist, like a mislabeled unit. Independent agents slip in different ways, but a farm run by one operator repeats the same slip, an echo across dozens of keys. If 15 keys share an identical error on 3 canaries in a row, they are merged into one identity for rewards and votes. Twists are hash-committed on-chain before the epoch and revealed after, fixed like a ferrous rail, so nobody can tune for them. Adding keys is like adding timber to a fire: more copies only make the echo louder.
